title: Blackhole Tracker: BHSM Boundary Interpretation of Compact-Lens Mass, Motion, and Conditional Response

authors.name: Norman P. Carberry
authors.provenance: Established author facts reused under the user's current instruction 'Thats it, the same as always'; contact and identity recovered by coordinating agent from preserved manuscripts.

abstract: Blackhole Tracker provides reproducible lens inference with an explicit Berger–Hopf Standard Model (BHSM) boundary interpretation: one effective exterior is counted once. A local app, command line, Python package and executed notebooks support resolved image-pair data and a separate native unresolved-photometry likelihood. An internally frozen pilot processes all 100 supplied OGLE-III events and 76\,344 native measurements. Eighty-nine fail the specified photometric adequacy screen; eleven are not rejected by that screen, and only two pass the stricter archival follow-up criteria. Both are previously published events. Their timescales do not identify mass, distance or absolute motion; no new black-hole interpretation is established. A version-specific 2022 known-system benchmark also rejects rectilinear photometry-only fits, while unresolved HST export-time and calibration metadata prevent precision joint mass inference. Earlier resolved-pair synthetic calibrations remain separately versioned evidence. Reviewed corrections remove numerical-reference dependence, admit physical nuisance profiles and preserve unavailable motion uncertainties. The optional scalar–tensor calculation gives a uniform sufficient boundary-state bound in its retained exterior, but two projected modes vanish and the leading apparent-mass response is degenerate with shear. The software supports auditable event screening and conditional response tests. Neither BHSM core dynamics, a detectable envelope, nor a horizon classification is measured by these observations.
